_comment: Documented intentional divergences subtracted from the surface-parity diff buckets. `exports.missing` keys are upstream symbols knowingly absent from PSFlow's surface; `exports.extra` keys are PSFlow-only names that are intentional renames/idioms. Each value is the rationale shown in report.md. Genuine-but-tracked gaps reference a ticket. A NEW upstream symbol not listed here trips the parity gate.
_comment_stale: This file is the second implementation of a **region** (CONTEXT.md; the first is parity/system/regions.json), and the stale rule holds on both: an entry that no longer corresponds to a real difference FAILS. Permanent entries included — a permanent entry that stops matching means upstream changed or PSFlow gained the export, and either is worth hearing about. So a fix deletes its entry in the same commit; an entry outlives its cause by exactly one run. `_comment*` keys are prose and are not entries.
_comment_props: `props.<Type>` accepts four keys, all optional. `rename` maps an upstream member name to the PSFlow name standing in for it and is applied to the upstream set before diffing, so one entry cancels the divergence on both sides instead of leaving a missing row and an extra row that can drift apart; it goes stale when it stops cancelling anything. `missing` and `extra` are rationale maps in the same shape as `exports.*`, consumed by the same claim(). `drift` is report annotation only — it labels a member in the output and suppresses nothing — but a drift key naming a member neither side has is stale like anything else. Prop divergence gates CI as of ticket 071: anything not declared here fails `npm run parity:surface`. Note the comparison is name-only; see the limit documented in report.md.

missing.NodeAddChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`. TS exports each change as a standalone type; PS models them as one sum type (intentional).
missing.NodeRemoveChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`.
missing.NodeReplaceChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`.
missing.NodePositionChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`.
missing.NodeDimensionChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`.
missing.NodeSelectionChange: Constructor of the PS `NodeChange` sum type, reachable via `NodeChange(..)`.
missing.EdgeAddChange: Constructor of the PS `EdgeChange` sum type, reachable via `EdgeChange(..)`.
missing.EdgeRemoveChange: Constructor of the PS `EdgeChange` sum type, reachable via `EdgeChange(..)`.
missing.EdgeReplaceChange: Constructor of the PS `EdgeChange` sum type, reachable via `EdgeChange(..)`.
missing.EdgeSelectionChange: Constructor of the PS `EdgeChange` sum type, reachable via `EdgeChange(..)`.
missing.NoConnection: Nullary constructor of PS `ConnectionState`, not a standalone type — documented in src/React.purs header & ticket 054.
missing.ReactFlowActions: PS models the store's action half as constructors of `React.Store.Action.Action` — a sum type a pure reducer folds — rather than as a record of methods, so there is no record for this name to denote. Documented in src/React.purs's header. Intentional and final.
missing.BuiltInEdge: Upstream union of the four built-in edge variants, discriminated by a string-literal `type`. PS `Edge e` carries `type :: Maybe String`, so the variants are not distinct types to union — documented in src/React.purs's header. Intentional and final.
missing.BuiltInNode: Upstream union of the built-in node variants, discriminated by a string-literal `type`. As `BuiltInEdge`: PS `Node n` carries `type :: Maybe String` — documented in src/React.purs's header. Intentional and final.
missing.ResizeControlLineProps: Props of upstream's internal `ResizeControlLine`. PS has no such component: `nodeResizeControl` serves both variants off one `ResizeControlProps`, selected by its `variant` field, so a second props record would describe nothing that exists — documented in src/React.purs's header. Intentional and final.

_comment_shapes: `typeof`, arity and React wrapper kind of every value `index.js` publishes, compared against the vendored upstream's. Every entry must name the event that retires it — a boundary stage or a ticket — which is enforced, because this section is the per-stage progress ledger: `stage N is done` means deleting stage N's entries here leaves the gate green. Deliberately not scoped to the boundary manifest: a gate bounded by the conversion plan is invisible-by-construction outside it. Boundary stage 4 deleted eight of them in one commit — every component whose wrapper kind disagreed, in both directions: PSFlow dropping a `memo` upstream has (`Background`, `Controls`, `MiniMap`, `EdgeText`), PSFlow adding one upstream does not (`BaseEdge`, `ControlButton`), and the two that were missing a `forwardRef` and therefore accepting a `ref` and dropping it (`Panel`, `Handle`). The 10 left sort into three classes — the ref pair `ReactFlow`/`ReactFlowWithRef` (#27), five curried pure functions, and three `Function.length` artifacts on hooks that nothing retires.

shapes.ReactFlow: Upstream is a `forwardRef`, PSFlow a plain function — `ReactFlow` is not a drop-in for upstream's because it does not accept a `ref`. This is ticket #27, which a ~20-line scratch script rediscovered independently. Retired by #27.
shapes.ReactFlowWithRef: PSFlow-only, so upstream has no shape to agree with: it is the ref-taking wrapper that exists precisely because `ReactFlow` is not one. Retired by #27, which makes `ReactFlow` a drop-in and removes the reason for a second component.
shapes.getConnectedEdges: Curried: upstream takes (nodes, edges) in one call, PSFlow one argument at a time. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns: #62 found that stage 4's `edgeTypes` makes this reachable — a custom edge component's first line calls one of these — and recorded that the fifth stage is warranted.
shapes.getIncomers: Curried: upstream (node, nodes, edges), PSFlow one at a time. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns: #62 found that stage 4's `edgeTypes` makes this reachable — a custom edge component's first line calls one of these — and recorded that the fifth stage is warranted.
shapes.getOutgoers: Curried: upstream (node, nodes, edges), PSFlow one at a time. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns: #62 found that stage 4's `edgeTypes` makes this reachable — a custom edge component's first line calls one of these — and recorded that the fifth stage is warranted.
shapes.getViewportForBounds: Curried: upstream takes six arguments, PSFlow one at a time. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns: #62 found that stage 4's `edgeTypes` makes this reachable — a custom edge component's first line calls one of these — and recorded that the fifth stage is warranted.
shapes.reconnectEdge: Curried: upstream (oldEdge, newConnection, edges, options), PSFlow one at a time. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns: #62 found that stage 4's `edgeTypes` makes this reachable — a custom edge component's first line calls one of these — and recorded that the fifth stage is warranted.
shapes.useKeyPress: Arity only, and a `Function.length` artifact rather than a divergence: upstream's `(keyCode = null, options = {})` both have defaults, so it reports 0 where the crossed ps-flow hook reports the 2 parameters it actually takes. Boundary stage 3 (#56) crossed it; matching the 0 would mean hand-writing an `arguments`-reading wrapper per hook, which makes the function lie about its shape to gain agreement with a number. **No boundary stage retires this** — the finding is recorded on #22, and it ends only if ps-flow gives these parameters JavaScript defaults of their own.
shapes.useNodeConnections: As `useKeyPress`: upstream destructures its single parameter with a `= {}` default, so arity 0 is a `Function.length` artifact and not a nullary declaration. Crossed in boundary stage 3 (#56); **no stage retires this**, recorded on #22.
shapes.useNodesInitialized: As `useKeyPress`: upstream's `options` parameter has a default, so it reports arity 0. Crossed in boundary stage 3 (#56); **no stage retires this**, recorded on #22.

_comment_behavior: Behavior entries are keyed by `<export>.<difference-class>`, not export alone. If a fix changes the class without closing the difference, the old entry becomes stale and the new difference is unclaimed, so one known failure cannot hide another. Every reason must name the boundary stage that retires it. **Boundary stage 5 is now a decision, not a question**: #62 was asked whether the fourteen unconverted pure exports warranted a fifth stage and answered yes, because stage 4 crossed `edgeTypes` — a JavaScript consumer can now register a custom edge component, and the first thing such a component does is call `getBezierPath` or `getSmoothStepPath`, which throw. Ticket 082 owns the stage; every entry below is one of the differences it deletes.

functions.getBezierEdgeCenter.positional-array-ret: Returns a labelled record where upstream returns a positional array. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getBezierPath.throw-vs-return: Still consumes PureScript Position constructors, so the shared JS enum strings a custom edge component is handed throw before its labelled-record return is reached. One of the six that are actively broken from JavaScript rather than merely differently shaped. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getConnectedEdges.call-convention: Returns the next curried function instead of accepting both arrays in one call. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getEdgeCenter.positional-array-return: Returns a labelled record where upstream returns a positional array. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getIncomers.call-convention: Returns the next curried function instead of accepting node, nodes and edges together. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getNodesBounds.call-convention: Its first call returns a function for PSFlow-only lookup/origin arguments where upstream returns the bounds. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getOutgoers.call-convention: Returns the next curried function instead of accepting node, nodes and edges together. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getSimpleBezierPath.positional-array-ret: Returns a labelled record where upstream returns a positional array. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getSmoothStepPath.throw-vs-return: Still consumes PureScript Position constructors, so the shared JS enum strings a custom edge component is handed throw before its labelled-record return is reached. One of the six that are actively broken from JavaScript rather than merely differently shaped. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getStraightPath.positional-array-return: Returns a labelled record where upstream returns a positional array. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.getViewportForBounds.call-convention: Returns the next curried function instead of accepting all six upstream arguments together. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.
functions.reconnectEdge.call-convention: Returns the next curried function instead of accepting the old edge, connection, edges and options together. Retired by boundary stage 5, which ticket 082 owns.

extra.children: React children are an explicit record field in PureScript rather than an implicit JSX slot; upstream gets them from React.PropsWithChildren, which the TS extractor does not attribute to the xyflow sources.
extra.onScroll: Inherited by upstream from HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, which the extractor excludes on both sides by design; PSFlow must declare it explicitly to expose it at all.

drift.positionAbsoluteX: closed by ticket 069 — the xPos/yPos rename is fully ported; retained as a pointer to the upstream 12.3.5 name
drift.positionAbsoluteY: closed by ticket 069 — the xPos/yPos rename is fully ported; retained as a pointer to the upstream 12.3.5 name
